speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallett's Syndrome (Boerhaave Syndrome)

This diagnosis fits your presentation of forceful vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption followed by a choking episode, which can cause a spontaneous esophageal rupture. The subsequent chest pain and coughing are classic signs, and the normal cardiac workup we performed earlier supports this. We will need a CT scan of the chest to confirm the diagnosis and assess for mediastinal air or fluid collection.
